subject: maths

concepts.title: Exponential Notation
concepts.definition: A shorthand way to represent the repeated multiplication of a number by itself using a base and an exponent.
concepts.key_idea: The exponent indicates how many times the base is used as a factor.
question_patterns: Find the value of {base} raised to the power {exponent}
What is the base and exponent in {expression}?
Calculate the value of {base} to the power of {exponent}

solution_steps.explain: The base is the number being multiplied, and the exponent is the number of repetitions.

concepts.title: Multiplying Powers with the Same Base
concepts.definition: When multiplying two powers that share the same base, the exponents are added together while the base remains unchanged.
concepts.key_idea: Addition of exponents for products of identical bases.
question_patterns: Express the product of {base}^{m} and {base}^{n} as a single power
Find the resulting exponent when multiplying {base}^{m} and {base}^{n}

solution_steps.explain: Since the bases are the same, the product's exponent is the sum of the individual exponents.
The result is the base raised to the new sum of exponents.

concepts.title: Dividing Powers with the Same Base
concepts.definition: When dividing powers with the same base, the exponent of the divisor is subtracted from the exponent of the dividend.
concepts.key_idea: Subtraction of exponents for quotients of identical bases.
question_patterns: What is the value of {base}^{m} / {base}^{n} in exponential form?

solution_steps.explain: The exponent of the result is the difference between the dividend exponent and the divisor exponent.
The result is the base raised to the calculated difference.

concepts.title: Power of a Power Rule
concepts.definition: To find the power of a power, multiply the internal exponent by the external exponent.
concepts.key_idea: Multiplication of exponents when a power is raised to another power.
question_patterns: What is the power of {base}^{m} raised to {n}?

solution_steps.explain: The resulting exponent is the product of the inner and outer exponents.
The base is raised to the product of the exponents.

concepts.title: Multiplying Powers with Different Bases but Same Exponents
concepts.definition: If two different bases are raised to the same exponent, their product is equal to the product of the bases raised to that exponent.
concepts.key_idea: Bases multiply while the common exponent remains the same.
question_patterns: Express the product of {a}^{m} and {b}^{m} as a single power
Multiply {a} and {b} then raise to power {m}

solution_steps.explain: Since the exponents are identical, we multiply the different bases first.
The product of the bases is raised to the common exponent.

concepts.title: Zero Exponent Rule
concepts.definition: Any non-zero number raised to the power of zero is always equal to one.
concepts.key_idea: Zero power of any non-zero base is unity.
question_patterns: What is the value of {base} raised to 0?
Evaluate the expression where the exponent is zero

solution_steps.explain: Any non-zero base raised to the power 0 results in 1.

concepts.title: Powers of Negative One
concepts.definition: Negative one raised to an even power is positive one, and raised to an odd power is negative one.
concepts.key_idea: Parity of the exponent determines the sign of the power of -1.

solution_steps.action: Check if exponent is even or odd
solution_steps.explain: If n is even, result is 1. If n is odd, result is -1.

concepts.title: Standard Form (Scientific Notation)
concepts.definition: A way to write very large numbers as a decimal between 1.0 and 10.0 multiplied by a power of 10.
concepts.key_idea: The exponent n is one less than the number of digits to the left of the decimal point.
question_patterns: Convert the large number {number} to standard form

solution_steps.explain: Count the number of places the decimal must move to the left to leave one non-zero digit.
Divide the original number by 10 raised to the power n.
